Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis. It thrives in cool, wet spring weather when temperatures are between 10–24°C and moisture persists on leaves for 9+ hours.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit. Infected leaves may curl and fall prematurely.

treatments.ratio: Neem Oil : Water = 1:50 ratio (20ml per litre)

prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn

Apple___Black_rot.cause: Caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa. Infects through wounds and enters bark during warm, humid weather (24–29°C).
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular lesions on leaves with purple margins. Fruit shows 'frog-eye' leaf spots and eventually turns black.
prevention: Prune infected branches 15cm below visible symptoms

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Caused by the fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. Requires two hosts — cedar/juniper and apple trees — to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with tube-like spore structures underneath.
prevention: Remove nearby cedar/juniper trees if possible
Apply fungicides during orange jelly-mass stage on cedars

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Leaves appear green, vibrant, and free of spots or discolouration.
prevention: Continue standard care — balanced NPK fertilizer

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Plant looks healthy with vibrant foliage.

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.cause: Caused by the fungus Podosphaera clandestina. Favours dry conditions with high humidity, temperatures between 15–27°C, and poor air circulation.
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on young leaves, shoots, and fruit. Leaves may curl and distort.

treatments.ratio: 1 tablespoon per litre of water + few drops dish soap

prevention: Ensure good air circulation by pruning

Cherry___healthy.symptoms: Healthy, vibrant foliage with no visible lesions.

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.cause: Caused by the fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis. Favoured by warm (25–30°C), humid, cloudy weather with extended periods of leaf wetness.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.symptoms: Tan to gray rectangular lesions parallel to leaf veins. Severe infections can cause significant yield loss.
prevention: Crop rotation — avoid corn after corn

Corn___Common_rust.cause: Caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi. Spreads via airborne spores in cool (16–23°C), humid conditions with heavy dew.
Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Small, circular to elongated, brick-red pustules on both leaf surfaces.
prevention: Scout fields regularly during cool, wet periods
Apply fungicide at early disease onset

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Caused by the fungus Exserohilum turcicum. Favoured by moderate temperatures (18–27°C) and extended periods of humid weather.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long (2.5–15 cm), elliptical, tan-gray lesions on leaves. Can cause 30–50% yield loss in severe cases.

treatments.ratio: 1ml each per litre of water (tank mix)

prevention: Deep tillage to bury infected residue

Corn___healthy.symptoms: Tall, vibrant plants with dark green leaves.

Grape___Black_rot.cause: Caused by the fungus Guignardia bidwellii. Thrives in warm (21–26°C), rainy weather. Spores are released during rainfall.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular lesions on leaves with dark borders. Fruit shrivels into hard, black 'mummies'.
prevention: Start protective sprays at bud break

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Caused by a complex of wood-rotting fungi (Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, Phaeoacremonium spp.). Enters through pruning wounds in cool, moist conditions.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Interveinal leaf chlorosis with reddish-brown margins (tiger stripe). Fruit shows dark spotting. Vine may suddenly wilt and die (apoplexy).

treatments.ratio: Use only as prescribed by a licensed agronomist

prevention: Protect pruning wounds with sealant immediately
Delay pruning until late in the season

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Caused by the fungus Isariopsis clavispora (Pseudocercospora vitis). Spreads in warm, humid, rainy conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves. Severe infections cause leaf drop, weakening the vine.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves, no spots or discolouration.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Caused by the bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect. There is NO cure — infected trees must be removed.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetric yellowing (blotchy mottle) of leaves. Fruit is small, lopsided, bitter, and may have aborted seeds.

treatments.ratio: N/A — destroy and remove tree immediately
0.5ml per litre of water, soil drench

Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni. Spreads during warm (24–28°C), wet, windy weather.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn purple-brown. Fruit shows cracked, sunken lesions.
prevention: Reduce injury from wind and insects

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green leaves with no visible lesions.
prevention: Scout for bacterial spot after rain

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria. Thrives in warm (24–30°C), wet, stormy conditions. Spreads rapidly by rain splash.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that turn brown and scabby. Defoliation can occur.
prevention: Crop rotation — avoid peppers/tomatoes in same spot 2 years running

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant, dark green leaves with no blemishes.
prevention: Calcium-rich fertilizer to prevent blossom end rot

Potato___Early_blight.cause: Caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. Favours warm (24–29°C), dry days followed by wet nights with heavy dew. Commonly infects stressed or aging plants.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown, circular spots with concentric rings (target-board pattern) on older lower leaves. Causes premature defoliation.
prevention: Maintain plant vigour with balanced fertilization
Rotate crops — avoid planting potato/tomato in same area

Potato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans — the pathogen behind the Irish Potato Famine. Spreads explosively in cool (10–20°C), wet, humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked, pale green lesions on leaves that rapidly turn dark brown to black. White mold visible on leaf undersides in humid conditions.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Lush green foliage with no spots or wilting.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Healthy canes with vibrant green leaves.
prevention: Monitor for spider mites in hot weather

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Lush, trifoliate leaves with healthy coloration.
prevention: Scout for soybean aphid and soybean cyst nematode

Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Caused by the fungus Erysiphe cichoracearum and Sphaerotheca fuliginea. Thrives in warm (20–27°C), dry conditions with low soil moisture but high humidity.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces. Leaves turn yellow and die as disease progresses.

treatments.ratio: 1 tbsp per litre of water + 0.5ml dish soap
3g wettable sulfur per litre of water
1 tsp baking soda + 1 tsp soap per litre

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Caused by the fungus Diplocarpon earlianum. Favours wet, cool conditions in spring and autumn.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small, purple or reddish spots on leaves that expand into irregular scorched areas. Severe infections cause defoliation.
prevention: Apply straw mulch to reduce splash
Scout for two-spotted spider mites in hot weather

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas species. Spreads rapidly during warm (24–30°C), rainy, stormy weather via rain splash.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves, stems, and fruit that turn dark brown with yellow halos.

Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Caused by Alternaria solani. Attacks stressed, mature, or aging plants in warm (24–29°C), humid conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings and yellow halos on lower, older leaves. Lesions spread upward.

Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Spreads catastrophically in cool (10–20°C), wet, foggy conditions. Highly infectious — can destroy an entire crop in days.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaves/stems. White mold on undersides. Fruit develops dark, greasy spots.
prevention: Destroy infected plants — do NOT compost
Apply protectant fungicide before blight-risk weather

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Caused by Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum). Common in greenhouse tomatoes with high humidity (>85%) and poor air circulation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-green to brown velvety mold on underside.
prevention: Remove and destroy infected leaves immediately

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Caused by the fungus Septoria lycopersici. Most common after first fruit sets. Favours warm (20–25°C), wet, humid conditions.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and white/gray centers on lower leaves. Spreads rapidly upward.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.display: Tomato   Spider mites Two-spotted spider mite

Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Caused by the fungus Corynespora cassiicola. Thrives in warm, humid tropical and subtropical climates.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Circular lesions with concentric rings (target appearance) on leaves. Brown spots also appear on fruit and stems.
prevention: Avoid high humidity in greenhouse conditions

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: A viral disease (TYLCV) transmitted by silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). No chemical cure exists. Early detection and vector control are critical.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of young leaves. Stunted plant growth. Flowers and fruit do not develop properly.

treatments.ratio: N/A — remove and destroy infected plants to prevent spread

prevention: Use insect-proof nets for seedling nurseries
Do not plant near infected fields

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Caused by Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV), highly stable and spread by contact (hands, tools, insects). No chemical cure.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves. Leaves may be distorted or blistered. Fruit may be mottled.

treatments.ratio: N/A — remove and destroy infected plants immediately

prevention: Wash hands thoroughly before handling plants
Control aphids which can spread virus
Do not use tobacco products near tomatoes (related virus)

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous plant with deep green leaves and no signs of stress.
prevention: Scout weekly for early blight, late blight and pests
